rows.description: He hears criticism and demand, feels overwhelmed and goes quiet, plugs in earphones or leaves. He thinks he is avoiding a fight; she experiences it as being abandoned.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: His silence confirms her fear, so she pushes harder with longer texts, tears or accusations. The louder the pursuer, the further the withdrawer retreats, and each is sure the other started the loop.
graph_context: previous stage: Feeling flooded and withdrawing
next stage: Seeing the loop, not the villain

rows.subtype: Stage 5: Seeing the loop, not the villain [Response]
rows.description: In a calm moment they name the pattern together: "when I press, you go quiet, and when you go quiet, I press." The shift is treating the cycle as the enemy instead of each other.
graph_context: next stage: Softer ask and staying present
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Softer ask and staying present [Response]
rows.description: She says "I miss you and I am scared" rather than "you never talk"; he says "I need twenty minutes but I will come back" and does. Vulnerability replaces criticism, and reliability replaces silence.
graph_context: previous stage: Seeing the loop, not the villain

rows.subtype: Stage 1: Work stress and quiet distance [Receiver]
rows.description: A partner returns exhausted from a demanding job and wants only quiet. He does not intend rejection, but his partner reads the flat evenings as a sign that her presence no longer matters.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: She offers small bids: a joke, a question, a hand on his shoulder. When a bid is missed she feels a small sting, and after enough missed bids the requests turn into complaints.
graph_context: previous stage: Work stress and quiet distance
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: Hearing "you are never here" he feels like a failure at both work and home, so he shuts down, works late or scrolls his phone. Avoidance protects him from feeling inadequate.
graph_context: next stage: Resentment on both sides
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: She feels lonely and unchosen; he feels nagged and never enough. Each keeps a private story in which they are the one trying, and generosity toward the other grows thinner.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A close friend notices both are lonely and hurt, not uncaring. She gently tells each what she sees in the other, without taking sides, which lets both stop hearing the other as an enemy.
graph_context: previous stage: Resentment on both sides
next stage: Scheduled closeness and honest limits

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Scheduled closeness and honest limits [Response]
rows.description: They agree on a regular unhurried time and a clear way for him to say "I am spent, give me an hour, then I am yours". The pursuer gets predictability and the withdrawer gets space without guilt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
